svg.title: MSSP Shared-Savings Architecture
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-mssp-shared-savings-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: MSSP Shared-Savings Architecture; subtitle: Who the ACO answers to, and the number each party is measured on; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Medicare Shared Savings Program ACO; headcount: 541 ACOs in MSSP (2019); focus: Bill fee-for-service, clear the roughly 3% minimum savings corridor, and let quality set bonus size; spokes: role: Participating Physicians; type: Gainsharing partner; kpi: Split capped near 50%; metrics tiered at 85/90/95% (Fredrikson); role: CMS; type: Benchmark owner; kpi: At 2.5% savings the ACO gets 20% and CMS keeps 80% (Reyann Davis); role: Payer Input Validation; type: Clinical review; kpi: Third-party and payer figures validated before tiering any preferred network (Garrett Schmitt); role: Convener Network; type: ACO organizer; kpi: About $171 per beneficiary dispersed vs about $95 local (Health Affairs); caption: Contingent models get paid from measured results against a defensible baseline. In MSSP that baseline is the benchmark, and Health Affairs warns any benchmark can be gamed; Reyann Davis cites a one-time $250,000 upfront payment as an ACO.; assumptions note: About 160 participants in 2018 generated savings and got no check because of the minimum savings rate (COPE Health Solutions). Fredrikson's $100,000 bonus at 90% on-time starts died at about 87%, which is why tiers beat all-or-nothing triggers.; note: Attributed to Nolan Feeny (lKGpIaNHgRw), Reyann Davis (EotsrYaUjUs), Fredrikson (VMuMGmjYplc), Garrett Schmitt (UEDbkKJ-9Xk), Health Affairs (Zzb5OKFwcbg), and COPE Health Solutions (PDcTn9Sq3mg).
